proposed_widenings.name: environment_modification
proposed_widenings.justification: Passwall creates a traversable passage in a solid surface for a timed duration with a cleanup effect on expiry. No existing spell family models this: 'ongoing_effect' requires a roll or damage operation on creatures; 'activation' requires at least one attack_roll or save_gate phase; 'triggered_reaction' is reaction-shaped; 'anchored_trigger' waits for a creature-triggered event before firing. Passwall immediately manifests a terrain feature and holds it for the duration.
proposed_widenings.evidence: A passage appears at a point that you can see on a wooden, plaster, or stone surface (such as a wall, ceiling, or floor) within range and lasts for the duration. [...] When the opening disappears, any creatures or objects still in the passage created by the spell are safely ejected to an unoccupied space nearest to the surface on which you cast the spell.

proposed_widenings.name: object_surface attachment
proposed_widenings.justification: Passwall targets a point on a specific solid surface (a material-typed surface: wood, plaster, or stone). The existing 'location' attachment (door_or_window, from Alarm) is a closed enum that does not cover material-typed wall/ceiling/floor surfaces. A new attachment variant or a widened 'object' attachment with a surface-material filter is needed.
proposed_widenings.evidence: A passage appears at a point that you can see on a wooden, plaster, or stone surface (such as a wall, ceiling, or floor) within range

proposed_widenings.name: on_expiry cleanup: eject_occupants
proposed_widenings.justification: When the passage expires, creatures and objects inside are safely ejected to the nearest unoccupied space. This is a deterministic cleanup behavior tied to the lifecycle 'expire' atom, but no existing lifecycle atom or effect covers spatial ejection of occupants from a created zone. The v4 'fall_on_end' and 'return_on_end' atoms are directionally close but semantically distinct.
proposed_widenings.evidence: When the opening disappears, any creatures or objects still in the passage created by the spell are safely ejected to an unoccupied space nearest to the surface on which you cast the spell.

notes: Passwall is a pure terrain-modification spell with no combat resolution step. It creates an opening in a solid surface, holds it for 1 hour (timed, non-concentration), then expires with a deterministic ejection cleanup. The v4 'create_object' atom is a plausible leaf-node for the feature creation, but there is no spell family in the surface that hangs a standalone create_object effect on a timed duration without a combat resolution phase. A new 'environment_modification' family (or a new 'terrain_feature_creation' family) is needed at the SpellMechanics union level.
